digest.component_or_area: plan review sizing / escalation rung target resolution
propositions: Context limit escalation resolves rung targets from module constants only, ignoring the run's actual provider qualification, causing provider-qualified models to silently degrade to bare Anthropic ids

When model-class table is unconfigured and primary model is provider-qualified (e.g. bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0), the escalation loop assigns bare family names back to cfg.model, losing provider context and breaking provider isolation
The one-criterion Pass-1 retry entry rung named 'frontier' resolves to an Anthropic provider context and triggers bare-id substitution on the common retry path, not just rare deep escalations
A run with Bedrock-qualified model and untouched cfg.model_provider composes invalid ids like bedrock:claude-opus-4-8 when rung targets are bare Anthropic names
Rung target decisions must be scoped to the run's provider context; unnameable higher rungs from different providers should be dropped rather than crossed to avoid provider escape

Provider-agreement rule between primary and target models ensures escalation stays on the operator's configured provider while preserving byte-for-byte back-compat for Anthropic-qualified or unqualified primaries
